name: S&P 500 Put Expiration Timing
claim: Returns from shorting out-of-the-money S&P 500 put options are concentrated in the few days before expiration.
quote: We document empirically that the returns from shorting out-of-the-money S&P 500 put options are concentrated in the few days preceding their expiration.
mechanism: option expiration

rules.timeframe: last days of the front-month option cycle
rules.entry: Short out-of-the-money front-month put options during the last days of the cycle; exact entry not stated

claimed_result: Returns are concentrated in the few days preceding expiration; a numerical value is not stated.

name: Goldman Roll Spread Pressure
claim: WTI calendar spreads narrowed during the commodity index roll window. The paper describes entering a short near-month and long deferred-month spread before the roll and unwinding it during the roll.
quote: The only difference is that Strategy 1 front-runs the Goldman roll by 10 business days, while Strategy 2 front-runs it by just 5 business days.
mechanism: Predictable index roll order flow pressures the spread between maturing and deferred futures.

rules.market: S&P GSCI energy futures, including WTI crude oil
rules.timeframe: Daily; positions held for 5 or 10 business days
rules.entry: Short the maturing contract and buy the deferred contract 5 or 10 business days before the corresponding roll date.
rules.exit: Unwind the spread on the corresponding index roll date.
rules.filters: Trade when the S&P GSCI rolls the commodity.

claimed_result: For 2000–2010, the paper reports 4.43% unlevered annual excess return for its energy portfolio under the 10-day strategy. For WTI, the reported difference between average roll yields in the first and last five days of the 15-day window was 0.47 percentage points.
required_data: S&P GSCI roll calendar and contract schedule

name: Funding Settlement Spot Spread
claim: Cryptocurrency spot quoted spreads are wider around perpetual futures funding times within the eight-hour funding cycle.
quote: Market makers respond to heightened adverse selection risk by widening quoted spreads.
mechanism: Funding settlement is associated with increased informed trading and wider spot bid-ask spreads.

rules.timeframe: Eight-hour perpetual funding cycle; hourly observations

claimed_result: Spot trading volume and percentage quoted spreads are larger around funding times than during normal hours.
required_data: Cryptocurrency spot bid and ask quotes

name: Dealer Gamma Intraday Price Dynamics
claim: Positive market-maker inventory gamma is associated with stronger intraday price reversal, while negative inventory gamma is associated with stronger intraday momentum in the S&P 500.
quote: We also show evidence suggesting that positive (negative) Market Makers’ inventory gamma strengthens intraday price reversal (momentum).
mechanism: Market makers' delta hedging of options inventory
claimed_result: Positive inventory gamma strengthens intraday reversal; negative inventory gamma strengthens intraday momentum.

name: S&P 500 option-expiration week effect
claim: S&P 500 returns averaged higher during weeks ending on the third Friday of the month than across all weeks.
quote: We nd that the mean return for the third Friday week is 37 basis points, more than double the average return for the full sample average of 15 basis points for all weeks.
mechanism: EVENT

rules.timeframe: Weekly, Friday to Friday; use the preceding available trading day when Friday prices are unavailable
rules.filters: Week ending on the third Friday of the month

claimed_result: July 1983–December 2008: mean third-Friday-week return was approximately 0.37%, versus 0.15% across all weeks; the reported spread versus other weeks was approximately 0.28 percentage points.

name: Bollinger Band Squeeze Breakout
claim: Narrow price action and shrinking Bollinger Bands indicate falling volatility, which IG says is often followed by a sharp rise; traders look for a significant breakout.
quote: Traders in this situation look for a significant breakout to signal a directional surge.
mechanism: VOL

rules.market: Almost any market; specific FX cross not stated
rules.entry: Look for a significant breakout after narrow price action and shrinking Bollinger Bands; exact entry not stated
rules.filters: Narrow price action and shrinking Bollinger Bands; thresholds not stated

claimed_result: Falling volatility is often followed by a sharp rise; no quantified result stated.

name: Bitcoin futures expiration week
claim: Bitcoin returns were positive in 65% of weeks containing a futures expiration and averaged five times the returns of usual weeks.
quote: The only case in which an anomaly was detected was related to abnormally high returns during the week of expiration: returns during such weeks were positive in 65% of cases, and were on average 5 times higher than during usual weeks.
mechanism: EVENT

rules.filters: Week containing a bitcoin futures expiration

claimed_result: In 2018–2021, 31 of 48 expiration weeks had positive returns; the paper reports a Sharpe ratio of 1.05 for its weekly simulation.

name: Option Expiration Week Effect
claim: Quantpedia describes a long S&P 500 timing strategy around the monthly option-expiration week.
quote: The research suggests that stocks with large market capitalization, that have actively traded options, tend to have substantially higher average weekly returns during these weeks.
mechanism: Event: monthly option expiration

rules.market: S&P 500, using SPY in the source
rules.timeframe: Daily closes; approximately one week holding time
rules.entry: Buy at the close on the Friday before the second Saturday of each month.
rules.exit: Sell at the close on the following Thursday.

claimed_result: For 1993–2019, the source reports 4.93% annual performance and 20.39% maximum drawdown for the SPY strategy.
required_data: S&P 500 index or index CFD price history

name: Quarterly Expiration Week Returns
claim: The S&P 500 averaged a loss during weeks containing quarterly triple-witching expirations.
quote: The S&P 500 has averaged a 0.53% loss during these weeks with 53% of the returns positive.
mechanism: Quarterly options and futures expiration

rules.filters: Weeks containing the third Friday of March, June, September or December

claimed_result: Average weekly return of -0.53%; 53% of weeks positive, using data since 2017.

name: Monthly Options Expiration Week
claim: Hold the S&P 500 during monthly options expiration week.
quote: Note that if we enter at the close of the trading week preceding the options expiration week, the average gain increases to 0.35% per trade.
mechanism: Monthly options expiration

rules.timeframe: Daily; approximately one week holding time
rules.entry: Buy at the expiration week's Monday open or the preceding week's close.
rules.exit: Close on expiration day, usually Friday; Thursday if Friday is a holiday.

claimed_result: Average gain of 0.35% per trade with entry at the preceding week's close; test period stated as after 1990.
required_data: S&P 500 index open and close prices

name: Nikkei ex-dividend recovery
claim: The Nikkei 225 shows an average recovery over the five business days after an ex-rights date.
quote: According to historical data, the average scenario is a recovery of about +0.7% within 5 business days after the ex-rights date.
mechanism: Dividend-related selling and subsequent reinvestment or dip buying
claimed_result: Average recovery of about 0.7% within five business days after the ex-rights date, based on eight occurrences from 2024 through June 2026.

name: Bitcoin high-funding fade
claim: Short Bitcoin when the last settled eight-hour funding rate exceeds 0.05%, and exit after seven days.
quote: BTC: short when funding > 0.05%, hold 7 days — +6.89%
mechanism: FLOW

rules.entry: Short when the last settled eight-hour funding rate is above 0.05%.

claimed_result: The BTCUSDT perpetual futures backtest reports +6.89% return, 63.97% maximum drawdown and 42 trades from 2020-01-01 to 2026-10-01. It includes fees, slippage and funding payments; these are not CFD results.

name: Bitcoin negative-funding long
claim: Buy Bitcoin when the last settled eight-hour funding rate is negative, and exit after seven days.
quote: BTC: long when funding < 0, hold 7 days — +333.12%
mechanism: FLOW

rules.entry: Go long when the last settled eight-hour funding rate is below zero.

claimed_result: The BTCUSDT perpetual futures backtest reports +333.12% return, 40.84% maximum drawdown and 155 trades from 2020-01-01 to 2026-10-01. It includes fees, slippage and funding payments; these are not CFD results.

name: Bitcoin top-decile funding weakness
claim: Bitcoin funding in the top decile of its own historical distribution was followed by a negative median 72-hour return.
quote: On BTC, top-decile funding was followed by a negative median return at 72 hours and a hit rate well below chance.
mechanism: FLOW

rules.entry: Funding reaches or exceeds the 90th percentile of its own history; a trade entry is not stated.
rules.exit: Price effect measured after 72 hours; a trade exit is not stated.
rules.filters: Funding percentile calculated using data available at the observation time.

claimed_result: Across 37 non-overlapping episodes from 2024-05-15 to 2026-07-13, the median 72-hour Bitcoin return was −1.18%; 40.5% of episodes ended higher.

name: Options Expiration Week Effect
claim: The S&P 500 gained an average of 0.35% per trade when entered at the close of the week preceding options expiration week.
quote: Note that if we enter at the close of the trading week preceding the options expiration week, the average gain increases to 0.35% per trade.
mechanism: EVENT

rules.entry: Buy at the close of the week preceding options expiration week.
rules.exit: Sell at the close of options expiration day, usually Friday; Thursday if Friday is a holiday.

claimed_result: Average gain of 0.35% per trade, or 35 basis points; test focused on the period after 1990.

name: DAX Before ECB Press Conference
claim: DAX open-to-close returns on the day before an ECB press conference show a positive drift.
quote: What is the main takeaway from our analysis?
mechanism: Pre-announcement drift

rules.entry: Buy at the open on the day before the ECB press conference.
rules.exit: Sell at the close on the same day.
rules.filters: Scheduled ECB press conference on the following day.

not_stated: return in basis points per event
claimed_result: The article reports positive performance during the open-to-close session on the day before the conference; basis points per event are not stated.

name: Closing Auction Indicative Price Reversion
claim: During US equity closing auctions, the indicative auction price tends to revert toward the continuous market's midpoint.
quote: Finally, we relate the dynamics of the indicative price to that of the limit order book: although the mid price does attract the indicative price, the latter fluctuates rather much and is not specially bound to be in the spread, which, we argue, is due to the sparseness of the auction order book.
mechanism: Auction order imbalance and indicative-price reversion

rules.market: US equities and ETFs, including SPY
rules.timeframe: Closing-auction period; exact trading window not stated

claimed_result: The paper reports that the indicative price reverts toward the regular order-book midpoint with non-negligible probability. It measures an indicative price, not an executed trading return.
required_data: contemporaneous best bid and ask prices

name: Futures Roll Spread Volatility
claim: In the study's U.S. equity index futures sample, calendar spread volatility rose as expiration approached.
quote: In the U.S., India, and China, spread volatility is confirmed to rise as expiration approaches.
mechanism: Position rollover flows concentrate in front-to-back futures calendar spreads as expiration approaches.

rules.timeframe: Daily; 15 trading days prior to and including front-month expiration

not_stated: magnitude of the U.S. spread-volatility increase
claimed_result: Spread volatility rose as expiration approached in the 2016 U.S. sample; the paper does not state a directional return in the quoted finding.
required_data: Front- and back-month S&P 500 E-mini futures prices

name: Option Inventory Shock Price Impact
claim: Large changes in option market makers' net delta positions are followed by S&P 500 futures returns in the estimated hedging direction.
quote: On the 5-minute frequency, we show that the largest absolute changes to the net delta position are followed by a reaction in the SPX futures return signed in accordance with the hedging direction.
mechanism: Option market makers hedge changes in their net delta exposure, creating price pressure in S&P 500 futures.

rules.filters: Largest absolute changes in market makers' net delta position; end-of-day window excluded in the reported analysis.

not_stated: specific threshold for a trading rule
claimed_result: Subsequent futures returns react in the estimated hedging direction; the cited passage does not state a basis-point effect.
required_data: Market maker option inventory or data to estimate it

name: FTSE Rebalancing Auction Short
claim: On index review event days, the FTSE 100 tends to fall into the closing auction print.
quote: The rule is as simple as the mechanism: on event days, sell in the last cash hour and buy back after the auction print.
mechanism: Index rebalancing flows at the closing auction

rules.entry: Sell 15 to 60 minutes before the cash close on an event day; exact entry minute not stated.
rules.exit: Buy back after the auction print; exact exit time not stated.
rules.filters: Trading day of the closing auction before the effective date of quarterly FTSE 100, STOXX or MSCI index reviews.

claimed_result: The source reports a net average of 11.5 basis points per event day across 27 holdout days from January 2023 to June 2026, assuming 1.5 index points per round trip.
required_data: FTSE 100 CFD intraday prices reflecting the auction print
FTSE 100, STOXX and MSCI index review dates

name: Thursday currency futures decline
claim: Foreign currency futures showed negative returns from 10:30 to 11:30 on Thursdays.
quote: For all five foreign currencies, there is a significant negative return from 10:30-11:30 on Thursdays.
mechanism: The paper associates the effect with dealers reducing foreign-currency inventory before U.S. money supply announcements.

rules.market: IMM futures on the Deutsche mark, British pound, Swiss franc, Japanese yen and Canadian dollar against the U.S. dollar

claimed_result: Significant negative returns for all five currencies during the specified Thursday hour in the 1977–1991 sample.

name: Closing auction indicative price reversion
claim: Before the closing auction, indicative auction prices tend to revert toward the continuous-market midpoint. The study includes SPY among the assets examined; it does not state a trading rule.
quote: Finally, the indicative price may be rather far from the mid price of the regular limit order book, although on average, the former reverts to the latter with non-negligible probability.
mechanism: FLOW: closing-auction order imbalance and its indicative price relative to the continuous-market midpoint

rules.timeframe: Pre-closing auction; exact entry and exit times not stated

claimed_result: The indicative price tends to revert toward the continuous-market midpoint; the quoted finding does not give a numerical reversion probability.
required_data: Historical closing-auction indicative prices and imbalance updates
Historical continuous-market bid and ask quotes

name: Xetra daytime auction price bounce
claim: Stocks with large price changes during the daytime auction exhibited a subsequent price bounce.
quote: Eventually, I find an after-auction return bounce for those stocks, whose price changed much during the auction.
mechanism: Potential liquidity-driven reversal following a daytime auction price change.

rules.market: German stocks traded on Xetra; the finding is not stated for the DAX index itself
rules.filters: Large auction price change; numerical threshold not stated

claimed_result: The reported regression coefficient for after-auction price change against auction price change is -0.061, with a t-statistic of -31.12.
required_data: Xetra stock prices immediately before, during and after the daytime auction

name: Threshold Rebalancing Price Pressure
claim: When stocks are overweight relative to allocation targets, institutional rebalancing is associated with lower next-day equity returns. The paper distinguishes an intra-month threshold signal from its month-end calendar signal.
quote: When stocks are overweight, funds sell stocks and buy bonds, leading to a decrease in equity returns of 17 basis points over the next day.
mechanism: Institutional portfolio rebalancing creates equity selling pressure when equity weights exceed targets.

rules.market: S&P 500 futures and 10-year Treasury note futures
rules.filters: Stocks overweight relative to target allocation

not_stated: threshold associated specifically with the quoted 17-basis-point effect
claimed_result: The paper reports a 17-basis-point decrease in next-day equity returns when stocks are overweight; its threshold signal also negatively predicts subsequent S&P 500 returns relative to 10-year Treasury note returns.
required_data: Portfolio allocation and rebalancing threshold assumptions

name: Futures Roll Spread Volatility
claim: S&P 500 E-mini calendar-spread volatility rose as contract expiration approached in the study's 2016 sample.
quote: In the U.S., India, and China, spread volatility is confirmed to rise as expiration approaches.
mechanism: Futures positions roll from the front contract to the next contract as expiration approaches.

rules.timeframe: Daily; 15 trading days up to and including expiration

not_stated: numerical magnitude of the volatility increase
claimed_result: The paper reports a statistically significant relationship between roll-period day and calendar-spread Parkinson volatility for the U.S. sample.
required_data: Front- and next-contract S&P 500 E-mini futures prices

name: Dealer Gamma Intraday Reversal
claim: Positive dealer inventory gamma is associated with stronger intraday price reversal; negative gamma is associated with stronger intraday momentum.
quote: We also show evidence suggesting that positive (negative) Market Makers’ inventory gamma strengthens intraday price reversal (momentum).
mechanism: VOL: market makers' delta hedging of 0DTE option inventory

rules.timeframe: Intraday; interval not stated in the abstract
rules.filters: Sign of market makers' inventory gamma

claimed_result: Positive inventory gamma strengthens intraday reversal, while negative inventory gamma strengthens intraday momentum; the abstract does not quantify either effect.

name: DAX Futures Expiry Opening Reversals
claim: Return reversals were significantly higher when a futures contract expired at the market open.
quote: Return reversals as the measure for the economic costs of contract expirations are significantly higher when a futures contract expires at the open.
mechanism: Futures expiration at the market open

rules.market: German stock index derivatives and underlying index stocks
rules.filters: Futures contract expires at the open

claimed_result: Significantly higher return reversals when a futures contract expired at the open; numerical magnitude not stated.
required_data: Intraday prices of the underlying index or stocks
Historical futures expiration dates and settlement times

name: Quarterly Expiration Opening Reversal
claim: Price reversals around the open on quarterly expiration days increased after index futures settlement moved to the open in June 1987.
quote: The results in Tables V and VI indicate that price reversals at the open on quarterly expirations increased significantly in the post-June 1987 period.
mechanism: Quarterly index derivatives expiration and settlement at the opening quotation.
claimed_result: Mean opening reversal for individual S&P 500 stocks rose from 0.061% before June 1987 to 0.281% afterward.
required_data: Intraday S&P 500 constituent stock prices around the open

name: ECB Fix Dollar Reversal
claim: The US dollar tends to appreciate before the ECB reference-rate fixing and depreciate afterward.
quote: This paper studies demand shocks for U.S. dollars in high frequency around currency fixings and documents a new empirical fact: the U.S. dollar systematically appreciates ahead of the three major currency fixings and depreciates thereafter.
mechanism: Dealer hedging and spot-market order imbalances around currency fixings.

rules.market: G9 currencies against the US dollar

claimed_result: The paper reports an average US dollar peak at the ECB fix, with appreciation beforehand and depreciation afterward; its full sample covers January 1999 through December 2019.

name: BOJ ETF Purchase Afternoon Effect
claim: A study cited by the Bank of Japan reports higher afternoon returns for Nikkei 225-linked ETFs on BOJ ETF purchase days than on other days.
quote: An early study by Ide and Minami (2013) focuses on the returns of ETFs linked to the Nikkei Stock Average (Nikkei 225) during the afternoon session, reporting that their returns during the afternoon session tend to be higher on days when the Bank of Japan purchased ETFs than they are on other days.
mechanism: EVENT: BOJ ETF purchases and afternoon returns

rules.filters: BOJ ETF purchase day; purchase trigger not stated

not_stated: availability of the purchase signal during the session
claimed_result: Afternoon returns tend to be higher on BOJ ETF purchase days than on other days; effect size not stated.
required_data: BOJ ETF purchase dates and signal availability

name: Monthly G10 Interest Rate Carry
claim: Sort G10 currencies by one-month interest rates, buy high-rate currencies and sell low-rate currencies, with monthly rebalancing.
quote: The portfolio composition is determined by sorting currencies on the basis of their prevailing 1-month LIBOR rate, and going long (short) currencies with the highest (lowest) interest rates.
mechanism: Currency carry from interest rate differentials

rules.entry: Go long high-interest-rate currencies and short low-interest-rate currencies, ranked by prevailing one-month LIBOR.

claimed_result: The spread-weighted portfolio had an annualized mean return of 5.21% from January 1990 through June 2012.
